A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–D. Added content and relocated or renumbered figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original toy-model simulations, MNIST training experiments, and evaluations of Pythia and OLMo checkpoints on FineWeb.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds input-covariance experiments and a linear-MSE control in Appendix D.6.

M1.justification: The proposed softmax teacher–student model, KL/cross-entropy objective, and aligned-student dynamics are unchanged. The new linear-MSE variant in D.6 serves as a comparison control.

E1.justification: v2 experimentally varied teacher-weight covariance but only discussed power-law covariance in Gaussian inputs. v3 actually evaluates the latter input-distribution scenario in D.6 and Figure 24. MNIST and FineWeb coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: D.6 adds an evaluated linear teacher–student comparator without softmax, trained using MSE between logits (Figure 25). v2 discussed MSE-based theories but did not report this control experiment.

E3.justification: The added D.6 experiments introduce normalized input-covariance sweeps and a control evaluated using logit MSE instead of distribution-matching KL divergence. These are protocols for added experiments; the stated settings of retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a robustness test of whether input-covariance spectra alter the 1/3 exponent and a control examining scaling after removing softmax and switching to MSE. These supplement the existing teacher-covariance and optimization analyses.

E5.justification: Existing fitted-exponent uncertainties and sampling descriptions are retained. The new D.6 plots introduce no additional repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-test reporting.

E6.justification: New Figure 24 reports convergence toward 1/3 scaling across input-covariance exponents. New Figure 25 reports exponential convergence near αx=0 and approximately 1/2 scaling for αx=2 under linear-MSE training. Existing plots and numerical findings are retained.

T1.justification: D.6 adds a linear-MSE loss formula and spectral derivation yielding exponent (αx−1)/αx for αx>1 (Equations 74–76). A.3 also corrects Equations 49–50 and their density assumptions to consistently refer to energy gaps.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and discussion retain the same claims about softmax/cross-entropy, peaked distributions, and universal intermediate-regime 1/3 scaling. The added experiments support existing claims.

C2.justification: D.6 adds interpretation of the linear-MSE control, contrasting covariance-dependent scaling with the energy-gap mechanism. It also attributes late deviations from the linear-model power law to finite input dimension. Existing broader limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the SVD-based input-covariance construction, normalization, and Gaussian sampling procedure, and adds implementation pointers to exp-5-2.py and exp-5-3.py. Existing implementation and code-access disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and Section 5 are unchanged. The added linear-MSE control illustrates the previously stated contrast with data-spectrum explanations without substantively revising the research positioning.

P1.justification: D.6 receives localized rewriting and expansion that distinguishes teacher covariance from input covariance. Minor wording edits occur elsewhere, while the overall section organization and main narrative remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 24–25, clarifies Figure 23’s teacher-covariance label, reduces the displayed sizes of Figures 10 and 17, and reflows appendix material. Former Figures 24–30 become Figures 26–32 with their underlying plots retained.

improvement.justification: v3 replaces a speculative input-covariance robustness argument with experimental evidence and adds a useful linear-MSE control and derivation. Together with the energy-gap formula correction, these strengthen support and clarity for the existing mechanism. Smaller appendix plots modestly reduce readability, and the broader alignment and gradient-flow limitations remain, but the net improvement is clear and limited.
